## Subjective

Mei-Ling Park, 34F, returns 3 days into productive cough w/ clear-yellow sputum (location: chest; quality: productive; duration: 3 days; timing: worse in mornings; modifying factors: minimal relief w/ honey-tea). URI symptoms (rhinorrhea, mild sore throat) resolving. Denies fever, dyspnea, chest pain, hemoptysis. PMH: HTN (controlled on lisinopril 10mg), penicillin allergy. Tobacco: never. EtOH: occasional.

## Objective

VS: BP 118/74, HR 88, RR 18, T 98.6°F, SpO2 98% on RA. Gen: NAD, alert, conversational. HEENT: mild posterior pharyngeal erythema, no exudate; TMs clear b/l. Lungs: scattered rhonchi b/l, clearing with cough; no wheezing or crackles. Cardiac: RRR, no m/r/g.

## Assessment

1. Acute bronchitis, viral etiology likely (J20.9)
2. URI, resolving (J06.9)
3. HTN, controlled (I10)

## Plan

Symptomatic care: hydration, rest, OTC dextromethorphan for cough. Albuterol HFA inhaler 1-2 puffs q4-6h PRN wheezing (limit 8 puffs/24h). F/u 7-10 days if symptoms persist or worsen. Continue lisinopril; recheck BP in 6 months. Patient education: viral URI, antibiotic stewardship discussed.
